nodes.name: NiFeCu alloy electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Before electrodeposition, the nickel foam was sonicated in concentrated HCl (37%) solution for 5 min to remove the NiOx surface layer, and subsequently rinsed with water and acetone, then allowed to dry in air. The electrodeposition was carried out with a standard three-electrode electrochemical cell containing nickel foam as the working electrode, a platinum foil (4 cm²) auxiliary electrode and an Ag/AgCl (3 M KCl) reference electrode. The electrolyte solution consisted of 80 mM NiCl₂·6H₂O, 25 mM Fe(NO₃)₃·9H₂O, 40 mM CuSO₄·5H₂O, 0.2 M sodium citrate tribasic dihydrate (Na₃C₆H₅O₇·2H₂O), 0.45 M ammonium sulfate ((NH₄)₂SO₄) and 0.55 M sodium hypophosphite monohydrate (NaPO₂H₂·H₂O). The electrodeposition solution pH was adjusted to 10.0 by 10 M NaOH solution. Typically, the NiFeCu alloy film was prepared through controlled potential electrolysis at -1.1 V vs Ag/AgCl at room temperature using a CH Instruments 660E potentiostat for 1 h. After deposition, the alloy was carefully rinsed with water and acetone.
nodes.source_text: Methods section: 'Before electrodeposition, the nickel foam was sonicated... After deposition, the alloy was carefully rinsed with water and acetone.'

nodes.name: CS-NiFeCu dealloying
nodes.procedure: The dealloying step was carried out in 3 M KOH with a controlled current density of 200 mA cm⁻² for 10 h. After dealloying, the CS-NiFeCu anode was withdrawn carefully from the electrolyte, rinsed with water and acetone, and then allowed to dry in air.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeCu alloy shows face-centered cubic (fcc) solid solution structure. CS-NiFeCu shows fcc peaks at 43.4°, 50.4°, 74.2°, 90.0°, 95.3° and weak CuO peaks at 35.6° and 38.9°, with amorphous NiFe oxides/hydroxides shell.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray powder diffraction (XRD) spectrum of NiFeCu alloy reveals that the as-prepared film formed a solid solution with a face-centered cubic (fcc) structure ... The XRD patterns (Supplementary Fig. 2) for the CS-NiFeCu catalyst show a series of peaks at 2θ = 43.4°, 50.4°, 74.2°, 90.0°, and 95.3° ... Two weak diffraction peaks of CuO at 2θ = 35.6° and 38.9° were observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeCu alloy shows dendritic structure with branches of 1.5-3.0 μm diameter. CS-NiFeCu maintains similar dendritic morphology with porous oxide shells.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM images observe that NiFeCu alloy uniformly deposited onto the nickel foam substrate with a dendritic structure (Fig. 1a) with clearly distinguishable hierarchy and tip-splitting ... The diameter of branches is distributed in 1.5-3.0 μm. SEM images show that the CS-NiFeCu electrode had a similar morphology compared with its parent alloy (Fig. 2a).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeCu alloy shows crystalline structure. CS-NiFeCu oxide shell is 250-300 nm thick with amorphous structure confirmed by lattice fringes and halo SAED pattern.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Magnified TEM image shows that the CS-NiFeCu oxides shell cover the branches with a thickness of 250-300 nm (Fig. 2c and Supplementary Fig. 5) ... High-resolution TEM image of CS-NiFeCu oxide shell show lattice fringes typical of an amorphous (disorder) material ... The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern of the shell is typically a halo feature.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeCu alloy has Ni:Fe:Cu = 10:1:21 atomic ratio. CS-NiFeCu bulk is Ni:Fe:Cu:O = 10:1:16:3; oxide shell debris is Ni:Fe:Cu:O = 10:1:10:26.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDS analysis of the bulk CS-NiFeCu catalyst shown an elemental composition (atomic) of Ni, Fe, Cu, O at Ni:Fe:Cu:O = 10:1:16:3 ... oxide shell debris was selected for further EDS analysis ... showing an atomic proportion of Ni:Fe:Cu:O = 10:1:10:26.

nodes.characterization_summary: CS-NiFeCu surface shows Ni²⁺ (2p₃/₂ at 855.7 eV), Fe³⁺ (2p₃/₂ at 710.8 eV), Cu²⁺ (2p₃/₂ at 934.1 eV), and metal oxide O 1s at 530.6 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the XPS spectra, Ni shows a distinct 2p₃/₂ peak around 855.7 eV ... Iron shows a fairly broad Fe 2p₃/₂ peak around 710.8 eV ... The main Cu 2p₃/₂ peak (934.1 eV) ... The main peak in the O 1s spectrum was at 530.6 eV, attributed to metal oxide.

nodes.characterization_summary: CS-NiFeCu shows Ni L₂,₃-edge similar to NiO (divalent Ni), Fe L₂,₃-edge matching high-spin Fe³⁺ in octahedral coordination like Fe₂O₃, Cu L₂,₃-edge with 19.7 eV splitting similar to CuO plus metallic Cu contribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The CS-NiFeCu is nearly identical to NiO apart from a slight broadening, which suggests that the oxidized Ni at the surface is primarily divalent Ni²⁺ ... The CS-NiFeCu is very similar to Fe₂O₃, showing the characteristic absorption profile of high spin Fe³⁺ ... Our measurements show the L₃–L₂ splitting is 19.7 eV for CS-NiFeCu, which is similar to the L₃–L₂ splitting in CuO.

nodes.characterization_summary: CS-NiFeCu shows double-layer capacitance Cdl of 54.24 mF cm⁻² from capacitive current vs scan rate plots, used to represent ECSA which is 9.3-fold higher than NiFe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 5a, the linear slope (Cdl) of CS-NiFeCu electrode has a value of 54.24 mF cm⁻², 9.3-fold higher than that of NiFe LDH under the same conditions.
